column1: 16:1|I commend to you our sister Phoebe, who is also a deacon of the church in Cenchreae.|Keeps Phoebe's kinship and named church ministry.

16:2|Welcome her in the Lord in a manner worthy of the saints, and assist her in whatever matter she may need from you, for she has been a benefactor of many people, including me.|Preserves welcome, practical assistance, and Phoebe's patronage.
16:3|Greet Prisca and Aquila, my fellow workers in Christ Jesus.|Keeps Prisca first and names both coworkers.
16:4|They risked their own necks for my life. Not only I but all the Gentile churches give thanks for them.|Retains the bodily danger and broad gratitude.
16:5|Greet also the church in their house. Greet my beloved Epaenetus, the firstfruits of Asia for Christ.|Preserves the house church and firstfruits image.
16:6|Greet Mary, who has worked very hard for you.|Keeps Mary's labor and its recipients.

16:7|Greet Andronicus and Junia, my relatives and fellow prisoners. They are outstanding among the apostles, and they were in Christ before me.|Retains Junia's feminine name, imprisonment, and apostolic prominence.
16:8|Greet Ampliatus, my beloved in the Lord.|Preserves the personal affection and relation in the Lord.
16:9|Greet Urbanus, our fellow worker in Christ, and my beloved Stachys.|Keeps both names and distinct relationships.
16:10|Greet Apelles, who is approved in Christ. Greet those from Aristobulus's household.|Preserves tested approval and the household group.
16:11|Greet my relative Herodion. Greet those from Narcissus's household who are in the Lord.|Keeps kinship and qualifies the household members.
16:12|Greet Tryphaena and Tryphosa, who work hard in the Lord. Greet the beloved Persis, who has worked very hard in the Lord.|Retains all three women and the intensified labor of Persis.
16:13|Greet Rufus, chosen in the Lord, and his mother, who has been a mother to me as well.|Preserves chosen status and Paul's familial extension.
16:14|Greet Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermes, Patrobas, Hermas, and the brothers and sisters with them.|Keeps every name and renders the mixed community inclusively.
16:15|Greet Philologus and Julia, Nereus and his sister, Olympas, and all the saints with them.|Preserves every named person and the surrounding holy community.
16:16|Greet one another with a holy kiss. All the churches of Christ greet you.|Keeps the embodied greeting and all the churches.

16:17|Now I urge you, brothers and sisters, to watch out for those who cause divisions and create obstacles contrary to the teaching you learned. Turn away from them.|Preserves the warning's objects, standard, and response.

16:18|For such people do not serve our Lord Christ but their own appetites, and through smooth talk and flattery they deceive the hearts of unsuspecting people.|Retains the belly idiom's appetite sense and the method of deception.

16:19|Your obedience has become known to everyone, so I rejoice over you. But I want you to be wise about what is good and innocent about what is evil.|Keeps public obedience, joy, wisdom, and innocence.
16:20|The God of peace will soon crush Satan under your feet. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you.|Preserves the peace/crushing tension and the pinned Christ reading.
16:21|Timothy, my fellow worker, greets you, as do Lucius, Jason, and Sosipater, my relatives.|Retains every name and distinguishes coworker from relatives.
16:22|I, Tertius, who wrote down this letter, greet you in the Lord.|Keeps the scribe's first-person identification.

16:23|Gaius, who is host to me and to the whole church, greets you. Erastus, the city treasurer, greets you, along with our brother Quartus.|Preserves hospitality, civic office, and all named greeters.
16:24|The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with all of you. Amen.|Follows the pinned main-text benediction and its inclusive scope.
